xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5211: Dashboard holds ~1.2 GB of one Codex transcript's tool output (screenshots) in memory

plan.title: Dashboard holds ~1.2 GB of one Codex transcript's tool output (screenshots) in memory
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The operator explicitly directed (2026-11-13, issue comment plus session instruction) that all five follow-up requirements ship in this issue. They share one foundation: the byte-level line splitter, record-offset sequences and historyStartOffset that the tail read, expand-by-offset, disk paging and the UI notice all consume, so a sibling split would land a bounded window with no way to page back past it. Most of the 35 files are paired test files; production logic lands in two new modules to respect the file-size ratchet.

narratives.Problem: The dashboard server held ~1.2 GB of one 1.6 GB Codex rollout's tool output (0.98 GB base64 PNG screenshots, 0.55 GB tool text) live in its heap, with RSS at 6.4 GB. The Codex accumulator stores every result whole, every multi-MB line is decoded and JSON.parsed whole so a cold open parses the entire file, the incremental reader and the snapshot cache budget file bytes and always keep one entry however large, and the output branch uses an O(n^2) workLog.indexOf lookup. The tool-body expand route reads the parse cache, not the transcript.
narratives.Proposal: Split transcript lines as bytes and scrub image data URLs to '[image: <format>, <N> KB]' before decoding or JSON.parse; skip lines over 8 MiB after scrubbing; open transcripts over 64 MiB by tail read. Cap every stored tool result at 65,536 characters (head and tail) through one helper used by Codex, pi, prime-agent, ohmypi and kimi. Budget the reader and the snapshot cache in retained characters (32 Mi total, 16 Mi hard per-entry cap) and give the Codex accumulator a 16 Mi/12 Mi window of newest rows. Number Codex rows by record byte offset, store each kept result's location so expand seeks straight to it, page older history back from disk, mark bounded windows so the conversation view shows a notice, and guard heap, peak RSS and cold-open time with a 200 MB synthetic transcript test. Keep Node's default heap limit (no --max-old-space-size) and document why.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Rendering images in the dashboard; image data is shown only as a placeholder.
- Capping tool-call arguments (detail, toolInput).
- Changing the Claude parser or its unresolvedResults.rawContent.
- Adding a byte budget to messagesCache in src/lib/overdeck/conversation-reads.ts.
- Full-text expand or disk paging for pi, prime-agent, ohmypi or kimi.
- Changing ACP's 500-character cap or the muse parser.
- Changing how Codex result JSON is displayed beyond the placeholder substitution.
- Setting --max-old-space-size on the dashboard.
- Changing transcripts-to-drive, appserver-events.jsonl, codex-home-v2 or embeddings.db.
- Raising any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap.

autoDecisions.summary: Image data URLs become placeholders everywhere, including expand and disk pages.
autoDecisions.rationale: The frontend has no input_image renderer (git grep finds none); base64 as text is useless and is the bulk of the memory.

autoDecisions.summary: Tool-body expand for Codex seeks to the record's stored byte location instead of reading the parse cache.
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified that both tool-body routes read the parse cache (conversation-reads.ts:702, agents/conversation.ts:291), so capping without a disk read would silently truncate expands; the operator's comment requires offset-based expand.

autoDecisions.summary: Codex row sequences and id suffixes become the record's byte offset when the reader supplies locations.
autoDecisions.rationale: Unique and ordered across the whole file regardless of tail-read start, which disk paging needs to continue the cursor; resume still works because offsets grow; costs one reset snapshot per open client after deploy.

autoDecisions.summary: Caps: 65,536 chars stored, 4 Mi chars on expand, 16 Mi retained per entry with a 12 Mi eviction target, 32 Mi total, 64 MiB tail read, 8 MiB parse limit.
autoDecisions.rationale: 16 Mi retained holds hundreds of capped results, far beyond the 75-row UI window; 4 Mi hysteresis limits window-slide resets; a 64 MiB tail of the sampled rollout yields roughly one window of rows.

autoDecisions.summary: pi, prime-agent, ohmypi and kimi get the text cap but not record locations or disk paging.
autoDecisions.rationale: They are whole-file re-parsers outside the incremental reader; results over 64 KiB are rare there and expand shows head, tail and an explicit omitted marker.

autoDecisions.summary: ACP and muse parsers are not changed.
autoDecisions.rationale: ACP already caps results at 500 chars (stricter than the helper); muse stores no work log.

autoDecisions.summary: The snapshot cache in shared-transcript-parser.ts is fixed here; messagesCache in conversation-reads.ts is a follow-up.
autoDecisions.rationale: The snapshot cache has the identical file-bytes and single-entry bug; conversation-reads.ts is at 989 of 1,000 lines and its entries are already bounded once Codex results are bounded.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not set --max-old-space-size on the dashboard.
autoDecisions.rationale: Default limit is 4,144 MiB per isolate on this host; this change bounds retained parse state by design, and a low cap turns transient spikes into a dashboard crash that drops every view at once.

autoDecisions.summary: The memory test measures heap after runtime-exposed gc, peak RSS and cold-open time, in a normal .test.ts file.
autoDecisions.rationale: Sliced strings can retain multi-MB parents invisibly to a byte-size assertion (probe: 127.6 MB vs 5.3 MB); runtime gc via vm.runInNewContext works in Vitest forks (probed); *.slow.test.ts is excluded from CI default runs.

autoDecisions.summary: The operator's follow-up comment is folded into this one plan rather than split into sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator explicitly asked to include all five follow-up requirements; recorded in plan.metadata.sizeJustification.
